clue.text: Feller has furniture stored away by house-builder

parts.note: lumber is disused furniture and junk put away in a lumber room
Jack is the builder in the nursery rhyme 'This is the house that Jack built'

explanation.surface: A tree-cutter keeps old furniture in storage beside a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like a casual word for a man, but it is one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberjack cuts down trees for timber, so he is a tree feller.

clue.text: University acts, indicating policy reversals

parts.note: acts on a variety bill are turns

explanation.surface: A university's actions point to a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a complete about-face, here in policy.

clue.text: Flashman's away to start game

parts.note: Flashman is the bully in Tom Brown's Schooldays
off means away, as in off on holiday

explanation.surface: The school bully leaves to begin a match.
explanation.walkthrough: Flashman is the bully of the Victorian school novel Tom Brown's Schooldays.
explanation.definitionFit: A bully-off begins play in hockey, two players clashing sticks over the ball.

clue.text: One's surrounded by queer people, considering

indicators.note: surrounded by means the single figure is enclosed by the two words that follow

parts.note: rum means odd or queer
a nation is a people
one is the Roman numeral I, with 's meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone, hemmed in by strange folk, is thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes between RUM and NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumination is deep thought, the act of mulling things over.

clue.text: Her bet is about to make a clear profit

indicators.note: is about means the stake word goes round the profit word

parts.note: an ante is a stake in poker
to net is to clear as profit after costs

explanation.surface: A woman's wager is set to pay off handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: NET sits inside ANTE. 'Her' only says the answer is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Annette is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: To chip stones sounds some game

indicators.note: sounds says the card game is heard, with a silent letter in the spelling

parts.note: nap is a card game, short for napoleon

explanation.surface: Breaking flints is said to be a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: The K is silent; NAP is a trick-taking card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To knap is to shape flint by striking off flakes.

clue.text: A superfluity of Jacobins

explanation.surface: Too much of a French revolutionary club.
explanation.walkthrough: In the French Revolution the radical Jacobins sat high in the Assembly and were called the Mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain of something is a huge excess; the Mountain was the radical faction of Jacobin deputies in the National Convention.

clue.text: Pusillanimously withdraw report of successful hatching

explanation.surface: Backing out in cowardice, or news that the eggs have opened.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the news that a young bird has emerged from its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out through fear is cowardly retreat; and a hatched fledgling is literally out of its egg.

clue.text: Hard to prohibit return of Biblical landowner, no salesman

indicators.note: return asks for the whole run of letters from 'Hard to prohibit' to be read backwards

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written
to prohibit is to ban

explanation.surface: Ancient rules forbid bringing back a land-holder who would not trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns HTOBAN backwards. In 1 Kings 21 Naboth refused to sell his vineyard to King Ahab, hence 'no salesman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naboth owned the vineyard King Ahab coveted, and he declined to part with it at any price.

clue.text: Exemplary soldier has leg broken by Varsity man in fun

indicators.note: in means the broken leg and the graduate are placed inside the word fun

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a broken leg has its letters smashed into a new order

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university graduate

explanation.surface: A model soldier fractures a leg while larking about with a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes GLE from LEG; GLE plus MA sits between FU and N of FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugleman was a well-drilled soldier placed in front of a company as a model for the others to copy.

clue.text: Tuneful Chopin miscellany with introductory note — top class

parts.note: E is a musical note, put at the start as 'introductory' says
U means upper class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: a miscellany is a mixed collection, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A melodious medley of Chopin pieces opens with a note of real class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miscellany' rearranges CHOPIN to PHONIC, after E and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphonic means pleasant-sounding, harmonious to the ear.

clue.text: Capital invested in Czechoslovakia?

indicators.note: invested in says the city lies buried inside the country's name

explanation.surface: Was money put into the former Czechoslovakia?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money invested; it is a capital city, found inside czechOSLOvakia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Old scholar's terms for "fixations"

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
academic terms are sessions

explanation.surface: A former student's terminology for obsessive interests.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, for 'old boy', is a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessions are fixed ideas that dominate the mind.

clue.text: Joined together but utterly distinct

explanation.surface: Something both linked and completely separate.
explanation.walkthrough: The contradiction is the trick: one sense is jointed, the other is clearly spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulate means jointed, linked by joints, and also means spoken clearly and precisely, each syllable distinct.

clue.text: Vehicle for sale?

explanation.surface: A car that is being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the legal transfer of property, the deed by which a house sale is completed.
explanation.definitionFit: A conveyance is any means of transport, and also the legal deed transferring property to a buyer.

clue.text: Too much trouble for ref in action

indicators.note: in places the troubled letters of ref inside the lawsuit

parts.note: an action at law is a suit

indicators.note: trouble for means the word ref is stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A referee gets more than enough grief during play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble for' makes RFE from REF, set inside SUIT. 'action' looks like sport but is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excess, more than is needed.

clue.text: Engineers (two military, one civil) used to manufacture bats once

indicators.note: two means the military engineers' letters are written twice

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army's engineers
MICE is a Member of the Institution of Civil Engineers

explanation.surface: Army and civilian engineers once made bats.
explanation.walkthrough: RE RE then MICE. 'once' marks the answer as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reremice is an archaic plural for bats, the flying mammals.

clue.text: Prospero's brother named after Venetian merchant?

explanation.surface: A character from The Tempest takes his name from a Venetian trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Shakespeare characters share the name: Prospero's usurping brother in The Tempest and the title merchant of The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest the usurping Duke of Milan is Prospero's brother; in The Merchant of Venice the merchant bears the same name.

clue.text: Obtain decoration or title, not without official lead

parts.note: taken as written
a title is a name

indicators.note: without means a letter is taken away from the word not

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: lead means the opening letter of official

explanation.surface: Get an honour or a title, but not without an official at the head.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O, the first letter of official, from NOT leaves NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is something added for adornment.

clue.text: Id put up with numbers of every description

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: I'd taken as written
numbers is an old word for verses or poetry

explanation.surface: I would tolerate all kinds of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: DI then VERSE; 'numbers' are lines of poetry, not figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse means varied, of many different kinds.

clue.text: Treacherous rock in lake

explanation.surface: A dangerous stone sits in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: snake-like and so treacherous; a green mineral rock; and the lake in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine means snakelike and so treacherous, names a green mineral rock, and is the lake in Hyde Park, London.

clue.text: Sent out to a den of thieves, perhaps

indicators.note: out means the letters of sent are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched to a robbers' hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest can mean a hideaway or haunt of criminals, as in a nest of thieves.

clue.text: In Rome, clue for a little copper god

explanation.surface: A Roman detail that helps a junior policeman find a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: A clue is a lead, and alchemists called lead Saturn; 'In Rome' places the god among the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the alchemists' name for the metal lead (a lead being a clue for a detective), and the Roman god of agriculture.

clue.text: Sacrifice a little distance with a lot of trouble and start to experiment

parts.note: a means one, the Roman numeral I
mm, millimetre, is a tiny length

indicators.note: of trouble means the words a lot are thrown into confusion
start to means only the opening letter of experiment

explanation.surface: Making an offering costs a short trip, much bother and an experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of trouble' rearranges A LOT to OLAT; 'start to' takes E from experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as a sacrificial victim, especially by burning.

clue.text: That French back is a smart type!

indicators.note: back means the French word is read from its end

parts.note: cela is French for that

explanation.surface: That Frenchman returning is a clever fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, someone too clever by half.

clue.text: Boy gets money. I hear, by writing verse

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name

indicators.note: I hear says the money word is only heard, then spelt the French way

parts.note: dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A lad is paid for his poems, so someone has heard.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAUX is said like 'doe', the same as DOUGH, giving the French plural ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Rondeaux are short poems with a refrain, a fixed form of French verse.

clue.text: Creed with subtle points

parts.note: nice can mean subtle or finely distinguished, as in a nice point
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A belief system full of fine distinctions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' here is the old sense of precise, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nicene Creed is the statement of Christian faith from the Council of Nicaea.

clue.text: Pope on close terms with eastern orange girl

parts.note: Clement is the name of several popes
to be in with someone is to be on close terms

explanation.surface: A pontiff is friendly with an Eastern girl selling oranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orange girl' suggests a fruit seller; the answer is both a small orange and a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small citrus fruit, and Clementine is a girl's name, as in the song 'Oh My Darling'.
